limits: Synthetic sources in temporary directories: the SPEC-023 generic trace fixture and episodes built by system_one_shadow.build_episode; no real host transcript or System One store is read, and trace_adapter admits synthetic traces only, so real host transcripts cannot be read until a real-source admission exists. Recorded traces and episodes are content-free by contract, so host-transcript records carry tools and statuses, not prompts. The full System One isolation test is procedure_007 (T009). Loom carries no model text or reward, which the loss notes state. Refused content stubs carry no attempt, so content-refused is a run-level note. Redaction limits are those of procedure_003 and procedure_004.
outcome: passed: T007: lightning_adapter turns one attempt's SPEC-070 events plus its redacted content records into braid-lightning-triplet/v0.1 records, one per model_request, and braid-lightning-messages/v0.1 user and assistant turns; the committed Loom corpus becomes one triplet per strand and one system message per event. Every text is redacted with the run salt and post-scanned (redaction classes counted), and each record carries source, sourceSha256 and sorted loss notes. Rewards match by first-occurrence (nearest earlier unrewarded request) or first-sibling (others refused with reward-match); a second content record for one request is ignored with content-duplicate. Outputs are deterministic for the same inputs and salt. Without consent, or for an unlisted source, prompt, response and messages are null or empty with content-consent-required while rewards stay. An unparseable Loom stream or an unknown attempt is refused with source-invalid. Negative control: with redaction switched off a canary in a Loom label reaches the output and the clean check fails. T008: a recorded host transcript (trace_adapter.read_trace and import_trace) becomes one triplet per host turn, in the source's operation order, with its tool as the tool call, a salted turn pseudonym as attemptId (an email canary in the trace attempt id never reaches the output, with or without consent) and prompt-missing, model-text-unavailable and reward-unavailable notes, and one system message per turn whose losses are the triplets' non-reward losses. A System One day file is read through system_one_shadow.read_day, the reader report() also uses (opened read-only, each line through validate_episode; an invalid or torn line is skipped and recorded as episode-invalid), and becomes one triplet per episode (System 2 pairs as prompt, System One answer as response, reward-unavailable) and user and assistant messages. Both are redacted, consent-gated per source (the loss names the gate's refusal: content-consent-required or source-not-consented) and refused with source-invalid when the trace does not validate or the day file cannot be read (missing path, a directory, no path). The episode file's bytes, mtime and directory listing are unchanged after reading. system_one_shadow is imported on use, and importing the Lightning modules in a fresh interpreter loads no socket, asyncio, ssl, http or urllib.request module. Loom strand and operation ids are free text too (a key or a dotted name is a valid id): each id at a reference position of the view_loom data schema (strandId, parentStrandId, waitingOn, crossing left and right, wave strands, planned waves, hazard units) is named once per stream by the salted, domain-separated pseudonym strand-<hmac16>, and the same map names triplets and messages; other fields (reportId, planId, scheduleId, manifestDigest, labels, tool names) are not renamed. Colliding pseudonyms refuse the stream with source-invalid. Host-transcript turns keep turn-<hmac16>. The test builds the stream from dicts with a token, three dotted names placed only in waves, units, a strand id and a v0.2 waitingOn target, and none reaches an output; shrinking the renamed positions to strandId, dropping the list positions or the waves, or dropping the collision check each fail it.
